title: The 5 Biggest Trees on Earth, Ranked (#1's Trunk Weighs 1,400 Tons)

scenes.text: The five biggest trees on Earth by volume. All five are the same species, in the same state.

scenes.label: Stagg · 1,205 m³
scenes.text: Number five: the Stagg tree, in California's Alder Creek Grove. 1,205 cubic metres of trunk and a base 33 metres around.

scenes.label: Lincoln · 1,259 m³
scenes.text: Number four: the Lincoln tree, in Sequoia National Park. 1,259 cubic metres, 78 metres tall.

scenes.label: The President · 1,278 m³
scenes.text: Number three: The President. 1,278 cubic metres. Count its branches and it would move up to second.

scenes.label: General Grant · 1,320 m³
scenes.text: Number two: General Grant, in Kings Canyon. 1,320 cubic metres and nearly 82 metres tall.

scenes.label: General Sherman · 1,487 m³
scenes.text: Number one: General Sherman. 1,487 cubic metres, 84 metres tall, 31 metres around. The trunk alone weighs nearly 1,400 tons. Its biggest branch is two metres thick.

description:
The five largest trees on Earth, ranked by trunk volume. All five are giant sequoias in California.
General Sherman in Sequoia National Park holds 1,487 cubic metres of trunk, stands 84 metres tall and measures 31 metres around at the base; its trunk alone weighs nearly 1,400 tons. The Washington tree was number two until fire damage in 2003 knocked it out of the top 30.
Which giant tree have you stood under?
first_comment: Tallest is a different contest: coast redwoods grow taller than any sequoia, but with far thinner trunks. Which would you have put at number one, and what should we rank next?
